theses.title: Hold the 45/20/25/10 target mix
theses.statement: The Carter household's investable assets stay pointed at 45% US equity, 20% international equity, 25% bonds, and 10% cash until the down-payment window opens.

supporting.text: Cash is 34.05% of the demo portfolio against a 10% target, earning less than the bond index in this synthetic series.
In the demo risk model, the target mix finished ahead of the current mix with lower volatility over the backtest window.

challenging.text: A house purchase inside two years would argue for holding more cash than the target allows.

theses.revision_conditions: Revisit if the house timeline moves inside 18 months, if either earner's job changes, or if reserves fall below the $24,000 floor.

theses.title: Fund the reserve floor before new risk
theses.statement: Bank cash plus the money-market reserve stays between the $24,000 floor and the $42,000 ceiling before any contribution goes to equities.

supporting.text: Demo reserves stand at $31,500, inside the floor band, with the auto loan as the only liability beyond the cards.

challenging.text: Cash above the ceiling drags on the demo portfolio's return in every backtest year shown.

theses.revision_conditions: Revisit if monthly essentials move by more than 10% for two straight months, or if the childcare step-down arrives early.
